newsitem.title: FRANCE: Asbestos ban has little impact - St Gobain.
newsitem.headline: Asbestos ban has little impact - St Gobain.

text.p: A French law banning the use of asbestos in new buildings from January 1 will have little impact on French building materials company Saint-Gobain, a company executive said on Friday.

"It's a non-event," said the executive, who declined to be named. But the company would be closing one factory employing 240 near Tours, central France, which has annual turnover of between 300-400 million francs, he said.
The state published a long-expected decree on Thursday outlawing manufacture, import or export of most kinds of asbestos effective from the new year.
The government and building industry has been in talks since last July when the measure was proposed, the executive said. Saint-Gobain stopped all asbestos production in September, he added.
"We were not a big player in asbestos," he said. Saint-Gobain mixed asbestos with cement to make wave-shaped roof slates and coverings for houses and farm hangars.

The company has another product made of cement and glass fibre which, while not a substitute, could be used in similar applications. The aternative costs between 30-40 percent more than the discontinued product, he said.
